correctness.rationale: Definition 2.3 of the arXiv 2026 rank paper yields a necessary/sufficient 3-round condition: some a has both an outgoing b and incoming c with all four extension types at each ordered pair. At n=6 these conditions force outdegree(a)=3 and 2 simultaneously; the cited rank-three tournament H_3 on seven vertices supplies existence, with code 17 as an independent direct witness. Rank >=4 is impossible on seven because a 3-point marked substructure of rank >=1 would need eight more vertices. Exhaustive 2^21 labelled masks and all 5040 relabellings per representative yield 1,503,216 and 313. The group-order histogram satisfies orbit-stabilizer summation, the unlabelled total independently equals the McKay count 456, and a separate recursive implementation agreed on all smaller masks through n=5 plus deterministic n=6 and n=7 samples. Code and source paths are included in the same package.

The McKay seven-vertex tournament catalogue counts all 456 classes without computing the extension rank. Closest published-finding corpus findings address rank-three undirected graphs or directed colour-refinement, neither equivalent to the 3-round tournament-extension predicate. Actual searches for aliases, parameters and exact claimed counts did not retrieve this theorem; global historical priority remains a risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 rank-property theorem motivates finite-host size thresholds. The full first feasible layer at order seven is a natural nonarbitrary invariant, yielding 313 isomorphism classes with explicit symmetry and labelled multiplicity strata rather than merely exhibiting another rank-three tournament. A sharp lower threshold and complete first-layer finite classification are mathematically useful despite not asserting a larger-order theorem.
